subject: Using reactive function 'recursively' - updating data as many times as user presses action button

messages.author: ca64010bcfa409b2
messages.subject: Using reactive function 'recursively' - updating data as many times as user presses action button
parts:
Hi, 

Currently, the user can load data into my app. I want to have an option to perform certain functions to change this data as many times as the user requests. I then want to use this updated data in outputs, such as a  DataTable and plotOutput. 

I have used the reactive function successfully when widgets are updated. So, for example, I can change the data once with

data <- reactive({ foo(df, input$var1, input$var2) })

However, I want to have the ability to take my updated data, data(), and apply this reactive function to the new data each time, as many times as the user presses the action button. So if the user presses the button three times, I will apply foo() to df three times. Does this functionality currently exist in Shiny, and if so, how can I implement it? I haven't found it yet.

Thanks,
Sharon

messages.subject: Re: Using reactive function 'recursively' - updating data as many times as user presses action button
parts:
The way I implemented a similar functionality in my app is a bit more complex.  It would be great if somebody else will comment with their methods, especially if simpler / better than mine -:)

In my case, a number of things need to occur every time somebody press a Save button.

Shiny has an action button that is incremented by one every time it is pressed. This is how I check if it has been pressed:

observe({
    # this line of code covers the first occurrence
    if(is.null(input$saveButton)) { return() }
    # this is to get the value of the button, but 
    # actually do something only when it has been pressed (+ 1)
    if(input$saveButton < valPpu$buttonF) { return() }
    valPpu$buttonF <- valPpu$buttonF + 1
})

Please note that valPpu is a reactive variable.  I use it to build "flags" that will be read by other part of the app (other reactive or render functions).

A render function depending on the button will look like:

output$xyz  <- renderSomething({
if(is.null(input$saveButton)) { return() }
  .... more code here ...    
 if(input$saveButton < valPpu$buttonF) {
 # ignore: the button has not been pressed!
....  more code here
} else {
# This will make sure this part of the code is not run next time
valPpu$buttonF <- input$saveButton
....  more code here
})

This makes the rendering function to react when the button is pressed, but making sure that any action is performed only once.

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: Using reactive function 'recursively' - updating data as many times as user presses action button
parts:
You could do something like this, where df is stored outside the reactive and modified each time:

df <- NULL
data <- reactive({
  df <<- foo(df, input$var1, input$var2)
  df
})


A more properly reactive solution would use reactiveValues. A reactiveValues object is just like the input object, so when you change values in it, it will invalidate all downstream reactives and cause them to re-execute:

vals <- reactiveValues()
vals$df <- NULL

observe({
  v$df <<- foo(isolate(v$df), input$var1, input$var2)
})

# Then you can access v$df as just like an input$xx value
output$table <- renderTable({
  v$df
})


Here's a working example of the latter, using an actionButton:

shinyApp(
  ui = bootstrapPage(
    actionButton("goButton", "Go!"),
    tableOutput("table")
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {
    vals <- reactiveValues()
    vals$df <- data.frame(x = numeric(0), y = numeric(0))
   
    # Add observer to watch for changes to input$goButton and update vals$df
    observe({
      vals$df <<- rbind(
        isolate(vals$df),
        data.frame(x=input$goButton, y=input$goButton)
      )
      # Need to isolate vals$df so we don't end up in infinite loop with vals$df
      # triggering this observer over and over.
    })
   
    # Then you can access vals$df as just like an input$xx value
    output$table <- renderTable({
      vals$df
    })
  }
)

-Winston
